summary:
## 🌟 Summary
**Ultralytics 8.4.198 makes training settings and YAML files more reliable, alongside fixes to downloads, dataset errors, and documentation.** No model architecture or pretrained-weight changes are included.

## 📊 Key Changes
- **NumPy learning rates now save correctly in YAML** — The main change converts `np.float64` values to ordinary numeric values when writing YAML. Training arguments such as sweep-generated learning rates can now be saved and reused from `args.yaml`.
- **More robust YAML parsing** — Fixes handling of block-scalar indentation, whitespace-only lines, and nodes written on their own lines, bringing the built-in parser closer to YAML conventions.
- **Improved download and dataset errors** — Downloads now identify themselves with an Ultralytics User-Agent, helping avoid some servers rejecting requests. Missing classification datasets now produce a clear file-not-found error instead of a confusing failed-download message.
- **More dependable training and logging** — Updates the minimum supported versions of `ultralytics-thop` and `ultralytics-platform`; also suppresses a Triton warning that could appear during profiling.
- **Clearer documentation** — Explains how relative `project` paths are resolved and standardizes how metrics such as mAP and depth accuracy are written across docs and benchmark tables.

## 🎯 Purpose & Impact
- 🔁 **Reuse training configurations more easily:** NumPy-based hyperparameter sweeps no longer produce YAML values that reload as strings and fail validation.
- 🧰 **Fewer confusing failures:** YAML parsing, downloads, and missing-dataset handling are more predictable.
- 📚 **Easier to follow guidance and compare results:** Consistent metric labels and clarified path behavior reduce ambiguity.
- ✅ **No model migration needed:** These updates improve tooling and documentation rather than changing model behavior.

## What's Changed
* Document that a relative `project` goes under `runs_dir/<task>` by @Echoslayer in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26985
* Fix block scalar indentation, space-only lines and own-line node indents in the YAML parser by @cainiao33 in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26987
* Remove UTF-8 BOM handling by @glenn-jocher in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26988
* Silence Triton 3.9 FP fusion default warning from torch 2.15 eager bmm by @glenn-jocher in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26989
* Write every metric with explicit sub/superscripts: mAP<sub>50-95</sub>, δ<sub>1</sub>, mAP<sup>val</sup><sub>50-95</sub> by @glenn-jocher in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26990
* Require ultralytics-thop>=2.2.4 and ultralytics-platform>=0.1.102 by @glenn-jocher in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26991
* Send a descriptive User-Agent on downloads and report missing classify data clearly by @glenn-jocher in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26992
* `ultralytics 8.4.198` Save NumPy float64 values as numbers in YAML files by @Nikhi00718 in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26993


**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/compare/v8.4.197...v8.4.198
title: ultralytics/ultralytics v8.4.198 - `ultralytics 8.4.198` Save NumPy float64 values as numbers in YAML files (#26993)

summary:
## 🌟 Summary
**Ultralytics 8.4.197 makes AMP checks work without downloading model weights and removes PyYAML from the base dependencies.** 🚀

## 📊 Key Changes
- **AMP checks no longer download a checkpoint.** The check builds an untrained YOLO26n from its YAML config and compares FP32 and AMP results across convolution and attention layers.
- **AMP checks are more independent of training setup.** They check the model’s device without relying on pretrained weights, internet access, or resetting callbacks.
- **Ultralytics now includes its own minimal YAML reader and writer.** It supports the YAML structures commonly used in Ultralytics configs, datasets, and export metadata. PyYAML is no longer a required base dependency.
- **Documentation examples now use `ultralytics.utils.YAML`** to save YAML files.

## 🎯 Purpose & Impact
- 📴 **Smoother offline training:** AMP checks can run without downloading weights, avoiding unexpected network requests and skipped checks.
- 🛡️ **More reliable AMP validation:** Comparing individual layers helps identify precision issues before AMP is used for training.
- 📦 **Simpler installation:** Removing PyYAML from the base requirements reduces a dependency for standard installs. The built-in parser covers Ultralytics’ common YAML needs, but it is not intended to support every YAML feature.
- 📄 **More consistent YAML handling:** Users can use the same built-in utility to load and save supported Ultralytics YAML files.

## What's Changed
* Replace PyYAML with a minimal built-in YAML parser by @glenn-jocher in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26983
* `ultralytics 8.4.197` Check AMP on an untrained YOLO26n without downloading weights by @glenn-jocher in https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/pull/26967


**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/ultralytics/ultralytics/compare/v8.4.196...v8.4.197
